Kelvin finds the order one pad at a time. At each stage, a wrong guess costs him the hops back up to that point plus the hop onto the wrong pad.

**Finding pad i (i = 1, …, 10).** When he already knows pads 1 through i−1, there are 10 − (i−1) = 11 − i candidates for pad i. In the worst case he tries 10 − i wrong ones before the right one. Each wrong try costs (i − 1) hops along the known path plus 1 hop onto the wrong pad, so i hops.

Total hops spent on wrong tries:

Σ_{i=1}^{10} (10 − i)·i = 10·55 − 385 = 165.

**The final successful run.** Once the full order is known, he makes 10 hops across the pads and 1 hop to the far bank, which is 11 hops.

Total: 165 + 11 = 176.

ANSWER: 176
